$comment: Copy to one of two places, both yours and neither inside any clone: <config dir>/config.local.json for every repository you work in, or <config dir>/repos/<id>/config.local.json for the repository whose committed config carries that `id`. <config dir> is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/devbook when set, else %APPDATA%\devbook on Windows and ~/.config/devbook elsewhere. They merge over .devbook/config.json in that order, the later winning: objects key by key with this file winning — a phase entry field by field, so a `model` here leaves the committed `agent` standing — arrays replaced whole, and `gates` appended so an overlay can add a checkpoint and has no way of spelling the removal of one. `null` here means deliberately unbound, never delete. A phase map here may name only what it changes; the two below are complete and carry the cost profile the engine shipped with, as your own model and effort per phase — delete the entries you are happy to take from the repository. Six things it may not say: `id` (it is what found this file), `components` (a stamp is repo-scope), `policy.pr.required`, `policy.qa.ceiling`, `policy.gate.personalValidation`, and `policy.openspec.scenarios` — those describe what this repository produces rather than how your machine runs it. Everything else in bindings, phases, areas, and policy is yours to adjust, and `ext.<plugin>.<key>` is where a plugin remembers what is true of your machine — refused in the committed file, read by that plugin alone. Validate with tools/stack-config/check.mjs, which finds every layer on its own. Still no secret: a home directory is not private.
